the Cryptococcus adhesins are a heterogeneous group of molecules with different functions and mechanisms of action that are still poorly understood.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cryptococcus spp., in addition to their ability to form biofilms, have a variety of adhesins that allow them to adhere to biotic and/or abiotic surfaces.
Cryptococcus spp., in addition to having a capsule, have other adhesion mechanisms that are not exclusive to this fungal genus, and that these mechanisms are shared with other fungi.
the study of Cryptococcus adhesion mechanisms will contribute to our understanding of fungal biology and will provide novel insights into fungal pathogenesis and host-fungus interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the adhesion mechanisms of pathogenic Cryptococci are diverse and complex, and they are mediated by several cell-surface and secreted molecules that interact with a variety of receptors on host cells.
